map.summary: The document outlines requirements for accessing and reviewing NPW data through the FAST application. It describes Home Page access, dashboard filters and NPW table behavior, including record details, temporal-trace links, sorting, grouping, and validation statuses. The Analysis Page presents the selected NPW’s details, a variable table and chart, step-based temporal traces, reference-dataset metadata, and TPM validation actions. Variables are assessed against a 20% out-of-envelope threshold, with comments used to indicate justification; NPWs with no variables above the threshold are automatically assigned OK status.
map.short_description: Describes requirements for NPW access, dashboard review, analysis tools, reference data, and TPM validation.

sections.title: Agenda and document structure
sections.summary: The document opens with an agenda listing the Home Page, NPW Dashboard, and Analysis Page. The Analysis Page topics include the NPW table, variable chart, NPW information, filters, temporal traces, validation, dataset reference, and variable table.
sections.short_description: Introduces the NPW document and outlines the Home Page, Dashboard, and Analysis Page sections and their major components.

sections.title: Home Page and dashboard filters
sections.summary: The Home Page requirement is for TPM users to access NPW processed through the FAST application, potentially under the name “NPW validation.” Dashboard filtering requirements include selecting equipment and module, associating user profiles with a Fab and Workarea, allowing managers to review equipment support-request status across a workarea, selecting a date to load the last 24 hours, and displaying NPWs processed on the selected date for the chosen equipment and module.
sections.short_description: Covers access to NPW data and the equipment, module, user-profile, and date filters on the dashboard.

sections.title: NPW dashboard table
sections.summary: The table should include event start, product, recipe, strategy, material, Context ID, temporal traces, TPM validation, and validator. Event start represents the NPW processing time and uses ISO 8601. Product, recipe, strategy, material, and Context ID display the corresponding NPW details; the product’s expansion control reveals related NPW MaterialIDs, newest to oldest, for the same strategy, recipe, and product, including previous PM. Temporal-trace links open a new page for that NPW MaterialID. TPM validation reads detailed temporal traces, supports filtering by status, and displays only OK, NotOK, or Support Request; the validator column identifies the validator. Each row represents an NPW and its strategy/recipe/product. Records are ordered newest to oldest by event start, grouped by matching strategy/recipe/product, and only the newest matching NPW is displayed in the table.
sections.short_description: Defines the dashboard table’s columns, status and temporal-trace links, sorting, and grouping of NPW records.

sections.title: NPW information on the analysis page
sections.summary: The Analysis Page displays the selected NPW’s date and time, product, recipe, strategy, and material. Each value is read from the corresponding Event Start, Product, Recipe, Strategy, or Material field in the Summary table row associated with the link or button selected from the dashboard.
sections.short_description: Specifies the NPW details shown on the Analysis Page and their relationship to the selected dashboard row.

sections.title: Variable table on the analysis page
sections.summary: A variable table lists all variables linked to the selected NPW Material ID, ordered from highest to lowest average out-of-envelope percentage (OOE%). It includes variable name, criticality, OOE%, worst-step OOE%, and comments. Clicking a variable name shows its temporal trace. Criticality values are limited to C1, C2, C3, C4, or undefined. OOE% and worst-step OOE% are compared with the reference population and use red above 20% and green below 20%. The comments field lets TPM users enter comments.
sections.short_description: Describes variable-table content, ordering, criticality and OOE indicators, trace links, and TPM comments.

sections.title: Variable chart on the analysis page
sections.summary: A circle chart shows the proportion of good variables, bad variables without justification, and bad variables with justification. Good variables fall below the 20% out-of-envelope threshold. Bad variables are above the threshold and are categorized according to whether comments are present in the corresponding variable-table Comments field. The total number of variables appears in the center of the chart.
sections.short_description: Defines the chart’s variable categories, the 20% OOE threshold, and its total-variable count.

sections.title: Temporal traces on the analysis page
sections.summary: The Analysis Page displays temporal traces for a variable selected in the variable table. Traces are delimited by Step ID and show the proportion of OOE by step. The reference-population envelope is blue, the reference trace green, out-of-envelope data pink, unqualified traces black, and qualified traces yellow.
sections.short_description: Specifies how selected-variable traces, step-level OOE proportions, and reference and qualification traces are presented.

sections.title: Dataset reference on the analysis page
sections.summary: The Analysis Page displays the reference dataset and its active version, number of contexts, last update, and envelope timeframe.
sections.short_description: Lists the reference-dataset metadata displayed on the Analysis Page.

sections.title: Validation on the analysis page
sections.summary: TPM users can validate the selected NPW. If no variables have OOE% above 20%, the NPW is automatically assigned OK status. The user can select OK, NOK, or Support Request. The corresponding buttons are colored green, red, and yellow, respectively.
sections.short_description: Covers TPM validation actions, automatic OK assignment, available outcomes, and button colors.
